summary: AE + SE walked Aurora Legal through Redwood's hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints, demoed search relevance workflow, discussed latency/cost tradeoffs and security (SOC2/ISO, KMS). Agreed to benchmark Redwood vs current stack using Aurora's 10k queries and to share pricing and security pack.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2028-11-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (Aurora - Head of Search), Mark Chen (Aurora CTO), Amir Khan (Aurora - Security)
Artifacts: redwood-hosted-demo-deck.pdf, relevance-benchmark-sheet.xlsx (link in chat)

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on the East Coast friendly time, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE, with Diego our solutions engineer.
00:08 Sofia: Hi, Sofia here, thanks. Mark and Amir are on as well.
00:12 Diego: hi all, quick agenda — show hosted embeddings, walk through rerank endpoint for search relevance, show console observability and then Q&A. Does that sound ok?
00:20 Mark: yep that's perfect. We're mainly curious about improving relevance for legal search and cost.
00:28 Maya: great, thanks. Quick qual — what does your current stack look like?
00:32 Sofia: we have Elastic for indexing, then we use Pinecone for vector store + an in-house reranker on top, it's a bit slow and pricey at scale.
00:41 Diego: got it. and what's your latency SLO for search?
00:44 Sofia: ideally sub-200ms for top-k responses, but right now tail is more like 600ms on heavy queries.
00:51 Diego: ok that's useful. Diego: (unclear) so in the demo i'll show embedding generation with our hosted endpoint and the rerank API which can do a coarse vector match then a hosted rerank pass to reorder results — all via single API calls.
01:05 Maya: moving into the demo deck — slide 3 shows the hosted API flow, we support batch embeddings, streaming generation, and a dedicated rerank endpoint that takes candidate IDs + text.
01:20 Sofia: can the rerank call do the heavy compute on our side? we have some private constraints around PII.
01:25 Diego: yes you can pass document ids and we fetch vectors if you store them in Redwood? or you can pass the full text as payload. For PII we recommend either private deployment or our hosted with encryption and SOC2 controls — we keep an audit log.
01:39 Amir: on that note, what's your data retention policy and KMS options?
01:42 Maya: we have customer-configurable retention windows, and KMS integration for dedicated/private. we'll share the SOC2 + ISO pack.
01:49 Amir: and SSO/SAML?
01:51 Maya: yes; SAML, SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC on Console.
01:55 Diego: jumping to the live demo — i'm going to call the embeddings endpoint with a sample legal paragraph.
02:05 Speaker 2: [typing noises]
02:10 Diego: ok sending request... response in ~120ms, here's the 1536-d vector (truncated).
02:20 Sofia: that latency is pretty good, what model are you running and is it quantized?
02:24 Diego: we expose a few model variants — for embeddings we have a higher-accuracy and a cost-optimized model; on our hosted tier we run mixed precision and some kernel optimizations. sometimes the transcriber shows 'Redwood Verified 1b' which is wrong, it's more like open model + kernel tuning.
02:38 Maya: now the rerank example — i'll show the flow: 1) coarse vector search in your store (we can integrate with Pinecone/Weaviate or use our in-built store), 2) call /rerank with top-k candidates and query, 3) response gives new scores and highlights.
02:55 Diego: i'm going to send their sample query set (small) through the rerank endpoint so you can see reorder and scoring.
03:10 [45 second demo running — some background typing]
03:55 Diego: results back — you can see the top candidate moved up, new score 0.92 vs previous 0.61, we also show token-level cost in Console.
04:10 Mark: can you show the Console cost breakdown?
04:15 Diego: yes — Console shows per-route cost, token counts, and a per-request latency histogram. we also surface rerank cost and per-candidate compute.
04:30 Sofia: our main worry is cost at 1M queries/day, how would hosted compare to our current Pinecone + in-house reranker?
04:39 Maya: good question — we typically run a sizing calc. For 1M q/day with average candidates 10 and 200 tokens per rerank, we estimate X cost; i'll send the detailed sheet. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization to reduce unit costs.
04:55 Amir: what's the SLA for hosted?
04:58 Maya: hosted has best-effort but we offer Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and a SLA; Dedicated also gives VPC/KMS options.
05:08 Mark: if we need VPC, how much lead time?
05:11 Maya: typically 2-4 weeks for private/Dedicated provision, depending on region and size.
05:20 Sofia: Diego, can rerank be run synchronously? we're worried about tail latency spiking.
05:24 Diego: yes, rerank is synchronous but we support async batch scoring and streaming. also prefix/KV cache can help for repeated queries. for tail mitigation we recommend canary routing and automatic fallback to a cheaper model if load spikes.
05:38 Sofia: do you support encrypted-at-rest with customer-managed keys?
05:41 Maya: yes for Dedicated/Private; hosted supports server-side encryption and we can discuss bring-your-own-KMS for enterprise.
05:50 Amir: any compliance certs?
05:52 Maya: SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 — will share the pack.
06:00 Diego: quick note — when integrating with Pinecone/Weaviate we just pull candidate vectors and call rerank; or you can push vectors into Redwood to simplify.
06:12 Sofia: how often do you refresh embeddings? we have heavy legal updates and doc churn.
06:17 Diego: depends on your pipeline; we support incremental re-embedding and partial updates. batching helps with cost.
06:25 Mark: ok, show us a benchmark comparison vs Pinecone + our reranker if possible.
06:30 Maya: that's the next step — we'll run relevance benchmark against your 10k set. Diego will drive the test and send results in a spreadsheet.
06:37 Sofia: timeline?
06:39 Maya: aim to have preliminary numbers in 48 hours.
06:42 [short side conversation about internal stakeholders]
06:58 Amir: question on logs — do you provide audit logs per request with payload redaction?
07:02 Diego: yes, audit logs with redaction options; you can turn on full request logging in Dedicated.
07:08 Sofia: any gotchas with GDPR/data residency?
07:11 Maya: hosted is region-aware, we have EU regions and can set retention/region. for strict residency we recommend Private.
07:20 Mark: what about competitor comparisons — how do you stack vs OpenAI embeddings + Pinecone?
07:25 Maya: we focus on production economics — we give more knobs for batching, caching, quantization and autoscale; that often yields lower unit costs in real workloads compared to naive hosted model + separate vector store.
07:38 Diego: and our rerank endpoint is tuned for low-latency reordering; we can show P95 numbers from previous benchmarks.
07:45 Sofia: ok this seems promising.
07:48 Maya: recap — we'll: 1) run benchmark with your 10k queries (Diego), 2) send pricing + dedicated sizing (Maya), 3) share SOC2/ISO + security pack (Maya), 4) schedule pilot kickoff w/c Nov 27 (Maya & Sofia).
08:05 Amir: sounds good. i just want to make sure the pilot covers security acceptance criteria.
08:10 Maya: absolutely, we'll include an acceptance checklist.
08:15 Mark: any blockers for us to run the benchmark?
08:18 Sofia: i'll upload the query set and a small doc dump to the shared drive after this call.
08:22 Diego: perfect — i'll pull it and run the job.
08:25 Maya: i'll follow up in email with the links and next steps.
08:30 [wrap up and thanks]
08:36 Sofia: thanks everyone, appreciate it.
08:38 Maya: thanks, talk soon.

Notes: transcription contains occasional recognition errors (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of KV cache). References to artifacts were shared in chat: https://redwood.example/hosted-deck (demo deck), https://redwood.example/benchmark-sheet (benchmark spreadsheet).
